visual_text: Melatonin: what to expect and what to ask
Slow-release, ages 55 and over, up to 3 months (European guideline)
Alzheimer's disease: may make little or no difference to sleep
Other sleep problems (adults and children together): about 7 minutes quicker to sleep, about 8 minutes more sleep, on average
What counts as success, and by when?
When will we stop or review?
Where does the product come from?
Riemann, J Sleep Res 2023; McCleery, Cochrane 2020; Ferracioli-Oda, PLoS One 2013
alt_text: Three columns on melatonin. What prescribed melatonin is for: slow-release, ages 55 and over, up to 3 months. What the evidence shows: little or no difference in Alzheimer's disease; about 7 minutes quicker to sleep and 8 more minutes in other sleep problems. What to ask: success, review, product source.
